title: Cavity Solitons
authors: W. J. Firth, G. K. Harkness
abstract: A driven optical cavity containing a nonlinear medium can support stable, soliton-like objects, bright non-diffracting spots of light on a uniform background. Importantly, the nonlinear medium need not support ordinary (propagating) spatial solitons, and cavity solitons have been both predicted and observed in a saturable absorber, and predicted to even exist in self-defocusing media. The history, present status, and physical interpretation of such cavity solitons is reviewed. Recent research predicts cavity solitons in semiconductor cavity models with properties interesting for applications to optical information processing. Cavity solitons are natural `bits' for spatial information, possessing both robustness and plasticity, and some potential applications of their unique properties are mentioned.
summary: This review surveys cavity solitons, stable light spots in nonlinear optical cavities, detailing their mathematical modeling using equations like the Lugiato-Lefever equation. The authors establish that these solitons possess unique robustness and plasticity, making them promising candidates for next-generation all-optical memory and processing units.
main_problem: The paper reviews the history, physical interpretation, and potential applications of cavity solitons—stable, bright, non-diffracting spots of light in driven optical cavities.
main_result: Cavity solitons can exist even when the nonlinear medium properties oppose those needed for standard Kerr solitons, suggesting they are robust candidates for all-optical information processing.
method: The analysis involves deriving and solving mean-field models, such as the Lugiato-Lefever equation, and performing stability analysis using Jacobian eigenvalues.
model_or_system: The system is a driven optical cavity containing a nonlinear medium, modeled by perturbed Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations (NLS) or the Lugiato-Lefever (LL) equation. These models describe the spatial evolution of light fields.
key_observables: Soliton stability (eigenvalues of the Jacobian), field profiles (localized spots), and the existence domain of stable solutions.
important_parameters: Linear loss ($\epsilon$), cavity mistuning ($	heta$), and pump intensity ($I$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on mean-field approximations, particularly the high-finesse assumption used to derive the LL equation from the full cavity dynamics.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic memory systems, Gaussian beam switching, bifurcation diagrams showing soliton states vs. parameters, and phase-plane plots confirming soliton stability regions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by reviewing the historical context (Stone Age to Information Age), developing the mathematical models (NLS to LL), analyzing the stability and physical interpretations of the solitons, and concluding with potential applications in all-optical processing.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics, as cavity solitons represent stable, localized excitations in nonlinear wave systems, analogous to engineered quantum states or information carriers.
